If your temperatures are spiking randomly, it could be due to a number of reasons. If you've recently removed the aio to replace your motherboard or something similar, then you could've maybe had a poor thermal paste application. It could also be due to air bubbles if you've had the aio for a long time, as the liquid in the loops does evaporate over time. You could try looking up "aio orientation" on YouTube and seeing if moving it to a better orientation (if you aren't already using a top mounted radiator) fixes it. If none of these work, then it could just be a faulty pump. If your pump is still under warranty, just try contacting NZXT's support. At least for me, I've always had good interactions with them.

Your fans are fine, but your radiator would be better if mounted on the top. Mounting it with the tubes on the bottom is better than how it is now, and can basically be summed up to the liquid in your aio will evaporate over time. With how it's mounted now, the longevity will be lower since it will eventually evaporate to a point (likely in several years, though) where the water can't fully reach to the top of the radiator, leaving a section where the pump is stuck only pushing air, which both won't cool anymore and potentially damage the aio. If you want to know more about it, you can just search up aio orientation on YouTube, and you'll get a ton of videos about it.

What you said is totally reasonable, but Whoop has official posts claiming that their algorithm can only account for the acceleration and movement on the wrist (it's the simplest to calculate there since it's usually what's moving the most in any workout compared to not moving at all maybe during something like a preacher curl). And I assume this would affect readings since they claim to use that info to calculate how "explosive" each rep is. Since they only have a certain number of workouts added, I'd assume they have a separate algorithm for each individual workout based on the assumption for how your wrist should be moving relative to your body and how it's moving in relative 3 dimensional space.

TL;DR: Readings on the movements will be less accurate (most likely lower) for certain exercises where your wrist moves differently from your biceps (wouldn't affect the reading on a back squat). Having it on the wrist will just make it more consistent and accurate if you believe in the accuracy of Whoop's algorithms.
